Fresh mathematical/literature audit verdict: thm:three-state-reduction is sound and has a short published-cardinality proof. The current obstruction overlooks the correct second variable.

Let R = (Y(0),Y(1)), taking four response-type values 00, 01, 10, 11. Start from any feasible witness Q with finite latent U. Conditional exchangeability is exactly A ⊥ R | U. Let J be Q’s full joint law of (A,R). The original U is therefore an admissible exact product-mixture factor for J, so the common entropy of J satisfies G_J(A;R) ≤ H_Q(U).

Now apply Kumar, Li, and El Gamal (2014) to the fixed pair (A,R), not merely to the observed pair (A,Y). Their Section V, Proposition 5 first gives finite attainment, and Proposition 6 states the general bound support(W) ≤ 2^{min(|A|,|R|)} − 1. Here |A| = 2 and |R| = 4, hence an entropy-minimizing factor W for the entire joint law J has at most three positive states. Therefore H(W) = G_J(A;R) ≤ H_Q(U) ≤ κ. The result is independent of the logarithm base because changing base multiplies every Shannon entropy by the same positive constant. Primary source: Kumar–Li–El Gamal, Exact Common Information, Section V, Propositions 5–6, https://arxiv.org/html/1402.0062.

Preserving J is stronger than preserving the six displayed moments. Explicitly, p00 = J(A=0, R∈{00,01}), p01 = J(A=0, R∈{10,11}), p10 = J(A=1, R∈{00,10}), p11 = J(A=1, R∈{01,11}), B = J(R=01), H = J(R=10). For every positive-mass state w of the new factor, set π_w = P(W=w), e_w = P(A=1|W=w), and r_{ij|w} = P(R=ij|W=w). Then A ⊥ R | W gives exactly the finite-factor product form. The six quantities above equal their original values because the complete joint law J is unchanged. Defining the observed outcome by consistency, Y = R_A, yields the original factual law P and the original benefit–harm point. Zero-mass padding gives an element of the three-state program. Thus every point in Θ_κ(P) belongs to Φ₃(F_{3,κ}(P)); the reverse inclusion already follows from lem:factor-program-equivalence.

The earlier six-state argument is valid but unnecessarily freezes the original conditional components and varies only their weights. General finite-moment extreme-point methods naturally support that style of reduction but do not exploit refactorization of the full joint law. Kumar–Li–El Gamal’s support-pattern argument changes the product components while preserving J and therefore reaches three states. Consequences: the locator should identify Section V, Proposition 6, not Proposition 2; the source proposition applies to arbitrary finite alphabets and depends on the smaller cardinality; treatment positivity is not used; no counterexample search is warranted; the support-three step is principally a direct corollary of a published result plus constructive causal completion, so standalone cardinality novelty should not be claimed; the representation blocker for dependent BH-CERT/contact obligations is removed but their singular termination and Hausdorff questions remain open.
